title: Study 1's sample
note: Figure 2(a) enrolls 334, 334, and 327, and the cleaned data and the rerun from raw exports both hold 995. The 988 is the pre-analysis plan's count, made by an earlier cleaning of a 2023-08-23 export. That export held only completed interviews, and the earlier cleaning dropped its first two data rows as if they were Qualtrics header lines, though they were two completed interviews that passed the attention check. The later exports also hold five partial interviews closed on 2023-08-24, and Study 2's cleaning keeps partial interviews too. Figure 7's Study 1 column was estimated on the 988-row file: 12 of its 48 labels move in the third decimal, and no sign or significance changes.

title: Two Study 2 index effects
location: p. 43, with the test on p. 39
published: Figure 7 shows that in Study 2, the effects on these post-treatment outcomes were also null
corrected: Figure 7 shows that in Study 2, the effects on these post-treatment outcomes were also null[[, save two pro-Democratic effects of about 0.01 on the 0-1 evaluation and identification indexes (one-sided p-values 0.019 and 0.011) that do not survive correction for multiple comparisons]]
note: Page 39 tests pro-Democratic effects one-sided at 0.025 in the pro-Democratic direction. On party ID that direction is down (1 = Strong Democrat), and on the two indexes it is up. The deposit's script took the lower tail for every pro-Democratic estimate, so on the indexes it tested the wrong direction and reported 0.981 and 0.989. The estimates are 0.010 (SE 0.005) on the evaluation index and 0.010 (SE 0.004) on the identification index, and the Benjamini-Hochberg p-value across the 96 tests is 0.435 for both. Party ID stays null, and Figure 7, which prints no p-values, is unchanged. Separately, the Study 1 script matches a label it has already renamed, so all 24 of its Pro-Democratic one-sided p-values are missing. With that repaired, the same page's "one significant result" among subgroups still holds, at 0.009.
